chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

If the young boy steals and has not yet reached puberty, his fingers are cut. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a boy who had stolen but had not yet reached puberty, so he cut the flesh from the tips of his fingers, then he said: If you return (to stealing), I will cut your hand.

key_terms.يَدَكَ: Your hand (referring to the full hand amputation)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a child who steals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific application of *qisas* (retribution) for juvenile theft, distinguishing between the partial amputation of fingers for a pre-pubescent child and the full hand amputation for an adult. It highlights the jurisprudential nuance that while the physical penalty is reduced for children due to their lack of full legal capacity (*bulugh*), the deterrent principle remains consistent, as demonstrated by Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) direct application of this ruling.
